aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abdon.title: Abdon
abdon.note: A Levitical town in Asher's territory, also written Ebron. It shows up in the allotment lists and barely anywhere else.

ahikam.title: Ahikam
ahikam.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahikam.note: A court official under Josiah. He backed the warnings of Huldah the prophetess and later protected Jeremiah from a mob that wanted him killed, and Gedaliah was his son.

amariah-6.title: Amariah
amariah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amariah-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

amon.title: Amon
amon.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amon.note: The son of Manasseh. He followed his father's early idolatry and never turned back, and his own officials killed him after two years. The people executed the plotters and made his young son Josiah king.

amoz.title: Amoz
amoz.about: Isaiah's father living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amoz.note: Isaiah's father, and not the prophet Amos: the names look alike in English but come from different Hebrew names entirely.

asahel-3.title: Asahel
asahel-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asahel-3.note: One of 4 men called Asahel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

asaiah.title: Asaiah
asaiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaiah.note: One of the officials Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah.

asaph.title: Asaph
asaph.about: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaph.note: A Levite David put in charge of one of the temple choirs. Twelve psalms carry his name, Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83, which means either he wrote them or a guild of musicians kept his name for generations.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

azaliah.title: Azaliah
azaliah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azaliah.note: Shaphan's father. Shaphan was the royal scribe who read the newly found Book of the Law to King Josiah.

azariah-8.title: Azariah
azariah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verses are 2 Chronicles 31:10 and 2 Chronicles 31:13.

azaziah-3.title: Azaziah
azaziah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azaziah-3.note: A Levitical name. One Azaziah was a musician under David; this one is an overseer in the temple stores.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

benaiah-8.title: Benaiah
benaiah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benaiah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

carchemish.title: Carchemish
carchemish.note: A major city on the west bank of the Euphrates. For a long time it was a Hittite provincial capital, and later the seat of a Neo-Hittite kingdom of its own. Nebuchadnezzar crushed Pharaoh Necho's army there.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

conaniah.title: Conaniah
conaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
conaniah.note: A Levite in charge of the tithes and offerings that came into the temple under Hezekiah's reforms.

cyrus.title: Cyrus
cyrus.about: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
cyrus.note: The Persian king who took Babylon and let the deported peoples, the Jews among them, go home and rebuild their temples. Isaiah calls him by name long before he was born, God's shepherd and anointed. The Cyrus Cylinder, found in Babylon in 1879, records the same policy.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

eden-4.title: Eden
eden-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eden-4.note: One of 3 men called Eden. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

eliakim.title: Eliakim
eliakim.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliakim.note: Hezekiah's palace administrator, sent with the other officials to talk to the Rabshakeh while Sennacherib had Jerusalem under siege. Another Eliakim was the king Necho renamed Jehoiakim.

eliel-8.title: Eliel
eliel-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliel-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

gihon.title: Gihon
gihon.note: Two waters carry the name. One is a river out of Eden that circles Cush and has never been matched to a known river. The other is Jerusalem's only natural spring, in the Kidron Valley, which Hezekiah ran underground into the city before Sennacherib's siege, and the tunnel can still be walked.

hashabiah-7.title: Hashabiah
hashabiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hashabiah-7.note: One of 10 men called Hashabiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

hasrah.title: Hasrah
hasrah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hasrah.note: Huldah the prophetess was his wife, and Josiah's officials went to her when the Book of the Law was found. He kept the vestments, and Kings spells him Harhas.

heman.title: Heman
heman.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
heman.note: David put him among the chief musicians over the worship, a Levite. Psalm 88, one of the darkest laments in the book, is credited to him.

hezekiah.title: Hezekiah
hezekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hezekiah.note: One of Judah's few good kings. He came after Ahaz, reopened the temple, tore down the high places, and broke up the bronze serpent Moses had made once people began worshipping it. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC, Hezekiah prayed, Isaiah promised deliverance, and the siege broke overnight. His seal impression has been dug up near the Temple Mount, and his tunnel still runs under the city.

hillkiah.title: Hillkiah
hillkiah.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hillkiah.note: The high priest under Josiah who found a forgotten scroll of the law while the temple was being repaired. What he found set off Judah's last great reform.

huldah.title: Huldah
huldah.about: Prophetess living at the time of Divided Monarchy
huldah.note: Josiah's officials took the scroll found in the temple to her, a prophetess in Jerusalem, and not to any of the men prophesying at the time. She told them it was genuine. Judgment was coming on Judah, she said, though not in Josiah's lifetime.

imna-3.title: Imna
imna-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
imna-3.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

ismachiah.title: Ismachiah
ismachiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ismachiah.note: In Hezekiah's reforms the temple filled with tithes and gifts, and Ismachiah was one of the Levites set over them, with Cononiah and Shimei, under the high priest Azariah.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jahath-4.title: Jahath
jahath-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jahath-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

jeduthun.title: Jeduthun
jeduthun.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
jeduthun.note: David put three chief musicians over temple worship, Heman, Asaph and Jeduthun. Several psalms carry Jeduthun's name in their headings.

jehiel-6.title: Jehiel
jehiel-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehiel-6.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

jehiel-7.title: Jehiel
jehiel-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehiel-7.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jehoahaz-2.title: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoahaz-2.note: Josiah's son. He reigned in Judah three months before Pharaoh Necho deposed him and took him to Egypt, where he died.

jehoiachin.title: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiachin.note: Three months on Judah's throne, then he surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and went to Babylon with much of Jerusalem's upper class. He spent thirty-seven years a prisoner. A new Babylonian king let him out and fed him at the royal table for the rest of his life, and 2 Kings ends there.

jehoiakim.title: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiakim.note: Pharaoh Necho put him on Judah's throne. When Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, he cut it off a section at a time and burned it in the fire pot, while his advisors begged him to stop. Jeremiah had it written out again, with more added.

jeiel-6.title: Jeiel
jeiel-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeiel-6.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jeremiah.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah.note: A priest's son from Anathoth, called as a young man in Josiah's thirteenth year. For four decades he told Judah Babylon was coming, and for that he was jailed, dropped in a cistern, and had his scroll burned. He saw Jerusalem fall as he had said, then was dragged off to Egypt against his will. His scribe Baruch may be the Berekhyahu on a clay seal from his lifetime.

jermoth-7.title: Jermoth
jermoth-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jermoth-7.note: A common name among Levitical families and men after the exile. This one appears once.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jeshua-4.title: Jeshua
jeshua-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeshua-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

joah-5.title: Joah
joah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joah-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

josabad-3.title: Josabad
josabad-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josabad-3.note: One of 9 men called Josabad. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

josabad-4.title: Josabad
josabad-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josabad-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

josiah.title: Josiah
josiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josiah.note: Made king of Judah at eight after his father Amon was murdered. In his eighteenth year workmen repairing the temple found a forgotten scroll of the law, and its reading set off Judah's last great reform: pagan altars torn down, the priests of the high places killed, and a Passover like none since the judges. He died young at Megiddo, trying to stop the Egyptian army reaching Assyria.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kohathites.title: Kohathites
kohathites.about: Levi's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kohathites.note: One of the three Levitical divisions, descended from Kohath. They carried the holiest furnishings, the ark among them, on poles and not in a cart, and 2 Samuel 6 shows what happened when that rule was broken. They camped south of the tabernacle. Moses, Aaron and Samuel were all Kohathites.

kore-2.title: Kore
kore-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
kore-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

maaseiah-7.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-7.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

mahath-2.title: Mahath
mahath-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mahath-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

manasseh-2.title: Manasseh
manasseh-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
manasseh-2.note: Hezekiah's son, who reigned in Judah longer than any king and did more harm than any. He rebuilt the high places, practiced sorcery, apparently sacrificed his own son, and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. Chronicles says captivity in Babylon broke his pride and he repented, but his reforms died with him.

megiddo.title: Megiddo
megiddo.note: It guarded the pass into the Jezreel Valley. A Canaanite royal city, it went to Manasseh and Solomon rebuilt it as a chariot city. Deborah and Barak beat Sisera on its plain, and King Josiah died there facing Pharaoh Necho, a death mourned so deeply it became proverbial. Thutmose III's siege of it around 1457 BC is carved in detail on the walls of Karnak.

merari.title: Merari
merari.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
merari.note: Levi's third son. His descendants had the heavy parts of the tabernacle, the frames, bars, pillars and bases, which went by cart instead of being carried.

meshullam-9.title: Meshullam
meshullam-9.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
meshullam-9.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

micaiah.title: Micaiah
micaiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
micaiah.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

miniamin.title: Miniamin
miniamin.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
miniamin.note: A priestly name of the years after the exile, carried by men who served in the temple and joined the dedication of the rebuilt walls.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nahath-2.title: Nahath
nahath-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nahath-2.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nebuchadnezzar.title: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuchadnezzar.note: King of Babylon. He destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off, and the Bible still calls him the tool God used to judge his people. Daniel tells how, after boasting of his greatness, he went mad and lived like an animal for seven years, until he gave God the glory and got his throne back.

necho.title: Necho
necho.about: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
necho.note: Necho the Second, pharaoh of Egypt, killed King Josiah at Megiddo. Afterwards he removed Josiah's son Jehoahaz and set up another son, Jehoiakim, under him.

nethaneel-7.title: Nethaneel
nethaneel-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaneel-7.note: One of 10 men called Nethaneel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

obadiah-10.title: Obadiah
obadiah-10.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
obadiah-10.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

ophel.title: Ophel
ophel.note: Temple servants lived on the Ophel, the fortified stretch of Jerusalem between the temple mount and the city of David, while Nehemiah was rebuilding the wall.

persia.title: Persia
persia.note: The empire that took Babylon under Cyrus. Unlike the empires before it, Persia let the exiled Jews go home and rebuild their temple, and Ezra keeps the decree.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

sennacherib.title: Sennacherib
sennacherib.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sennacherib.note: He besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's reign and boasted in his own inscriptions that he shut Hezekiah up like a bird in a cage. He never claims he took the city.

shallum-5.title: Shallum
shallum-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shallum-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

shecaniah-4.title: Shecaniah
shecaniah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shecaniah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.

shemaiah-14.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-14.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-14.note: 2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shemaiah-15.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-15.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-15.note: One of 26 men called Shemaiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 2 Chronicles.

shimeah-7.title: Shimeah
shimeah-7.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shimeah-7.note: 2 Chronicles names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

zachariah-15.title: Zachariah
zachariah-15.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-15.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verse is 2 Chronicles 34:12.

zachariah-16.title: Zachariah
zachariah-16.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-16.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. 2 Chronicles names him once.

zadok.title: Zadok
zadok.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
zadok.note: The priest who stayed with David through Absalom's rebellion. He would have carried the ark out with the king, and David sent it back. Zadok anointed Solomon, and when Abiathar backed Adonijah and was sent away, Zadok was left as the only high priest.

zedekiah.title: Zedekiah
zedekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zedekiah.note: The last king of Judah. Nebuchadnezzar put him on the throne, and he rebelled anyway, against everything Jeremiah told him. Jerusalem was destroyed, he was caught running, his sons were killed in front of him, and then they blinded him.
